lede.headline: Midterm wins for Democrats rattle AI data-center stocks
lede.dek: Dell and other server makers sank on Nov. 4 as investors weighed what a Democratic Congress, and a Texas governor who campaigned on a data-center moratorium, could mean for the AI buildout.

top10AsOf: List as of Sep 24, 2026 9:15 PM ET

stories.headline: Dell drops 8.3% as midterms raise data-center doubts
stories.move: Dell Technologies shares fell 8.31% on Nov. 4, TipRanks reported, after Democrats won control of the House and Senate in the Nov. 3 midterm elections. TipRanks said the result threatens political support for the AI data centers that buy Dell's servers, pointing to incoming Texas governor Gina Hinojosa, who campaigned on halting new data-center projects until more rules are in place. Reuters separately reported that data-center and chip stocks broadly fell that day on worries about tighter AI oversight under a Democratic Congress, even as the S&P 500 and Nasdaq closed higher.
stories.why: Dell's AI server business now drives most of its growth, so investors are pricing in the risk that a less AI-friendly Congress, plus state-level pushback like Texas's proposed moratorium, could slow the data-center spending behind it.
stories.bear: Even after the drop, TipRanks said Dell was still up 219.56% year-to-date, so the pullback erased only a small share of 2026's gains.
stories.watch: Whether other states follow Texas's proposed moratorium on new data-center construction.

stories.read: A reputational, not yet financial, headache
stories.headline: Nvidia's Huang asked to brief Congress on China ties
stories.move: Three House Republican committee chairs — Brian Mast, John Moolenaar and Rick Crawford — asked Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang in a Nov. 4 letter to attend a closed-door briefing on Nov. 18, CNBC reported. They cited reporting by The New York Times that U.S. intelligence determined a Chinese citizen and Megaspeed executive, Alice Huang, had passed information to Beijing, and that Jensen Huang had developed a close relationship with her. Nvidia told CNBC that such customer contacts are routine for a CEO and that it shares no sensitive trade secrets with regional cloud customers.
stories.why: The scrutiny lands days before Nvidia's Nov. 17 earnings and adds a national-security angle to the AI-chip story, even though Nvidia disputes any wrongdoing.
stories.bear: The committee chairs' letter does not name its underlying evidence, and Nvidia says the government would alert it if it believed any individual posed a real threat.
stories.watch: Whether Huang attends the Nov. 18 briefing and what, if anything, becomes public afterward.

stories.read: Biggest tech merger of the year, messy market reaction
stories.headline: Marvell's $115 billion Lumentum deal spooks investors
stories.move: Marvell Technology agreed on Nov. 2 to buy optical-component maker Lumentum Holdings in an all-stock deal with an implied enterprise value of $115 billion, the companies said in a joint press release. Lumentum holders will get a fixed 4.5 Marvell shares each, a 23.9% premium to the Oct. 28 unaffected price; Marvell holders will own about 67% of the combined company and Lumentum holders about 33%, with closing expected in the first half of 2028. Koch, Inc., the holding company run by Charles Koch, has reported owning Marvell shares in its 13F filings.
stories.why: Marvell's release cites a $550 billion addressable market and more than $1 billion in annual cost synergies, but Bank of America cut Marvell to Neutral from Buy and its price target to $225 from $400, citing possible selling pressure from the roughly 50% increase in Marvell's share count, financial news site goldesel.de reported.
stories.bear: Marvell says the deal should add to its non-GAAP earnings per share in the first year after closing, but the transaction still needs shareholder and regulatory approval, and BofA flagged that a long review could extend the stock overhang.
stories.watch: Shareholder and regulatory approval for the deal, expected to close in the first half of 2028.

stories.headline: AMD's data-center revenue nearly doubles in record quarter
stories.move: AMD reported third-quarter 2026 revenue of $13.4 billion, up 45% year over year, in a Nov. 3 earnings release. Data Center segment revenue hit a record $8.5 billion, up 97% year over year, while non-GAAP diluted EPS was $2.09, up 74%. Client and Gaming revenue fell 8% to $3.7 billion, and Embedded revenue rose 29% to $1.1 billion. Management guided to about $17 billion in fourth-quarter revenue, plus or minus 3%.
stories.why: AI chip demand for AMD's Instinct and EPYC lines is now outgrowing its legacy PC and gaming business, reinforcing AMD's position as a second major supplier alongside Nvidia.
stories.bear: Client and Gaming revenue declined, showing AMD's growth is increasingly concentrated in one segment.
stories.watch: Fourth-quarter 2026 results, expected early 2027, against the roughly $17 billion guide.

stories.read: A real beat, not just a bounce
stories.headline: Reliance stock jumps 11.6% on record quarterly profit
stories.move: Reliance Industries shares rose 11.60% to close at 1,300 rupees on the NSE on Nov. 2, its biggest single-day gain since April 2020, Business Today reported. Consolidated net profit for the July-September quarter rose 40.64% year over year to 25,548 crore rupees, and revenue rose 28.57% to 3,32,861 crore rupees. Telecom unit Jio Platforms reported revenue of 47,485 crore rupees, up 11.3%, with 542.4 million subscribers.
stories.why: The rally pushed Reliance's market value to nearly 17.6 lakh crore rupees and reinforced Ambani's position among Asia's richest people.
stories.bear: A single record quarter doesn't guarantee the growth rate holds, and part of the profit jump reflects an easier year-ago comparison.
stories.watch: Reliance's board-approved plan to raise up to 15,000 crore rupees via debentures, and Jio's long-delayed IPO.

stories.read: Growth mode, and the market liked it
stories.headline: Airbnb's fastest growth in years, plus a $12B buyback
stories.move: Airbnb reported third-quarter revenue of $4.869 billion, up 19% year over year, with gross booking value up 21% to $27.7 billion and nights and seats booked up 16% to 155 million, in its Nov. 4 earnings release. Net income was $1.89 billion. The board authorized an additional $12 billion in share buybacks, on top of $2.7 billion left from the prior program.
stories.why: CEO Brian Chesky called it a return to "growth mode" and the company raised its full-year guidance to high-teens revenue growth and about 36% adjusted EBITDA margin.
stories.bear: A one-time $135 million tax benefit lifted net income this quarter, which flatters the headline profit number.
stories.watch: Airbnb's guest-facing AI travel agent, planned for the first half of 2027.

stories.read: Revenue beat, profit missed, stock still rose
stories.headline: Uber beats on revenue as driver supply gets tight
stories.move: Uber reported third-quarter revenue of $14.77 billion, above the $14.69 billion analysts expected, but adjusted earnings of 25 cents a share missed the 96-cent estimate, CNBC reported on Nov. 4. Mobility revenue fell 2% to $7.52 billion, below estimates, while freight revenue rose 34% to $1.76 billion, beating estimates. Shares rose more than 7% that day.
stories.why: CEO Dara Khosrowshahi said elevated fuel prices and tighter driver availability weighed on supply growth in several international markets, and Uber is investing to add drivers in India, Brazil and the U.S.
stories.bear: Net income fell 92% from a year earlier, though the prior year included a large one-time tax benefit that makes the comparison hard to read either way.
stories.watch: Whether driver supply loosens in the fourth quarter as Uber's investment takes effect.

stories.read: A public OpenAI is getting closer
stories.headline: OpenAI president says it could be ready to go public in 2027
stories.move: OpenAI President Greg Brockman said at a Wall Street Journal tech conference in Napa, California on Nov. 4 that the company could be ready for an IPO in 2027 and that enterprise sales now make up the majority of its revenue, Reuters reported.
stories.why: A listing would be one of the largest tech IPOs ever and would give outside investors their first direct stake in OpenAI.
stories.bear: Brockman set no firm date, and OpenAI has pushed back its IPO timeline before.
stories.watch: Whether OpenAI sets a formal listing date in 2027.

watch: Nvidia's Q3 earnings, due Nov. 17, and Jensen Huang's closed-door Congressional briefing set for Nov. 18.
Whether other Democratic-led states follow Texas's proposed data-center moratorium.
Shareholder and regulatory approval for Marvell's Lumentum deal, expected to close in the first half of 2028.
memo: Political risk can move your stock fast: Dell fell 8.3% in a day after an election outcome changed assumptions about data-center demand — worth stress-testing how a policy swing could hit your own customer base.

A big acquisition doesn't guarantee a stock pop: Marvell fell on dilution worries even as its own leadership called the Lumentum deal earnings-accretive. Investors will do their own share-count math regardless of how you frame a deal.

A leader's outside relationships can become a company problem: Nvidia's CEO is being pulled into a national-security inquiry over a business contact, a reminder that executives' personal ties carry company-level risk.

movers.why: Dell fell 8.8% after Democrats won control of Congress, raising doubts about political support for AI data centers, TipRanks reported.
Marvell fell 7.1% after BofA cut it to Neutral, citing dilution risk from its $115 billion all-stock deal for Lumentum.
